title: The Benyuan Dharma Gate Is an Outer Path Attached to Buddhism
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Q: Is the Benyuan Dharma Gate an outer path attached to Buddhism?

inline.s: Q: Is the Benyuan Dharma Gate an outer path attached to Buddhism?

A: The Benyuan Dharma Gate is, of course, an outer path attached to Buddhism. What is meant by an outer path attached to Buddhism is one that adheres to Buddhism while distorting and tampering with its doctrine.

It exploits such weaknesses of human nature among the faithful as shrinking from difficulty, taking easy shortcuts, and clinging to worldly pleasures, in order to fool the faithful and cheat them of fame and gain
, and even to attain some political aim
The Benyuan Dharma Gate wholly fits this definition, so it is a genuine, out-and-out outer path attached to Buddhism.
An ordinary outer path attached to Buddhism raises the banner of the Dharma,
fools the faithful
in order to cheat them of fame and wealth, and even to attain some political aim.
But the Benyuan Dharma Gate goes far beyond this:
it seeks to destroy the true Dharma of the Buddha from its very root.
Therefore, besides having a systematic false teaching that distorts and tampers with Buddhist doctrine, it also incites the breaking of precepts and the doing of evil so as to wreck the sangha.
And through the so-called
“Triple Abolition and Establishment”
(see
“Appendix Five: The Triple Abolition and Establishment of the Benyuan Dharma Gate”
it slaughters those who differ from it in order to root out the true Dharma.
This is where the enormous harmfulness of the Benyuan Dharma Gate lies!

[Incite the breaking of precepts and doing evil to wreck the sangha] The Benyuan Dharma Gate holds that doing evil and committing crimes are all of no account, and that monks may take wives and eat meat. Its doctrinal canon, The Shinshu Doctrine, says:
“Though the offense of an ordinary person is great, compared with the power of the vow it is but a single grain in the vast ocean

(though the offense of an ordinary person is great, compared with the power of Amitābha Buddha’s vow it is like a single grain of millet compared with the great ocean — utterly insignificant. For the refutation of this fallacy, see
Appendix Nine:
Refuting “Recitation of the Name Surely Brings Rebirth” and “the Evil Person Is the True Capacity”
, so no matter whether a
(monk)
eats meat or keeps a wife.”

They loudly proclaim: no need for practice, no need to keep the precepts, no need to do good, no need to purify one’s own mind; even doing evil for a whole life is of no account, because the evil person is the true capacity whom Amitābha Buddha saves. For example, Master Huijing, in The Essence of Master Shandao, says: “One does not know that the purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to manifest Amitābha’s original vow: the evil person is the true capacity.” And Master Xinyuan, Master Huijing’s disciple who took refuge in him, in The Salvation of Amitābha Is the Evil Person as the True Capacity, says: “Let us now look at Amitābha Buddha’s salvation — with what kind of sentient being as its true capacity? The evil person as the true capacity.”

According to the Benyuan Dharma Gate’s topsy-turvy teaching, its incitement to break precepts and do evil, and its scheme to slaughter those who differ, while it abolishes the whole Path of Sagely Practice
(every method of practice other than the Pure Land Dharma Gate)

, it will also slander the earnest, single-minded Buddha-recitation that accords with the teaching as “self-power recitation” and abolish it. At that point the Buddhist fold becomes a single unified world for those who neither earnestly and single-mindedly recite the Buddha’s name, nor keep the precepts, nor cultivate merit, nor purify their own minds, and who may even do evil for their whole lives. Monks who eat meat and keep wives no longer shave their heads, and even the monk’s robe is laid aside for fear of public scrutiny when they break precepts and do evil. In this way, the true sangha that is the model for gods and men no longer exists, and the masses, unable to obtain the genuine Dharma and finding no fruit in their practice, lose faith in the Dharma. What a scene this is!
(This scene already has precedent; see
The Practice of the Teaching of Master Hōnen
When the cart ahead overturns, the cart behind takes warning!
[When the cart ahead overturns, the cart behind takes warning] When the cart in front overturns, the cart behind must take warning from it.
Q: Why must the Benyuan Dharma Gate be criticized?
A: Because the deeds of the Benyuan Dharma Gate possess the three great characteristics of
destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha
. First,
topsy-turvy teaching
, replacing the true Dharma with a false teaching

(they loudly boast that for rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss there is no “need to cut off evil and do good,” no “need to keep the precepts,” that “doing evil and committing crimes are of no account,” that “the evil person is the true capacity whom Amitābha Buddha saves,” that “recitation of the name surely brings rebirth,” that “the gate of the great vow,” and so on — see the several appendices and the further reading.)
. Second,
inciting the breaking of precepts and the doing of evil

, corrupting the fourfold assembly of home-leavers and householders, and in particular seeking to destroy the true sangha that is the model for gods and men, so as to extinguish the Buddha’s true Dharma
(see the several appendices)
The Buddha said:
“In the future the destruction of the true Dharma will not come from the assault of the demons and heretics, but precisely from the corruption and collapse of the sangha!”
(On the Sangha Jewel)
Third, the slaughter of those who differ and the monopoly of all under heaven
(see the section
“Triple Abolition and Establishment”
in the appendix)
making the Buddhist fold a single unified world of false teachings and evil persons.
In this way, the Buddha’s true Dharma is destroyed.
And the retribution for destroying the Buddha’s true Dharma is most painful:
whether the propagators of the Benyuan Dharma Gate, or their followers, patrons, and supporters
(the karmic guilt of these latter three kinds of persons is that of being the tiger’s ghost helper)
all will fall into the Avici hell for long kalpas.
Therefore, whether for the sake of protecting the true Dharma or out of compassion, the Benyuan Dharma Gate must be criticized,
so that everyone comes to know the truth.
(Those who deliberately do evil certainly deserve their retribution; but those faithful who are fooled and mistakenly board a pirate ship, and in a confused way follow them to create karmic evil
(destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha)
and receive retribution
(falling into the Avici hell for long kalpas)
, are truly pitiable and hardly worth it. O vast and boundless heavens, what manner of men are these!)
In the Buddha Treasury Sutra

in the chapter on ancient times, the seventh, the Buddha, when speaking of the retribution of those who in the past destroyed the true Dharma of the Buddha and of their followers, patrons, and supporters, says:
These evil persons,
destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha,

also bring great ruin and affliction upon many people. Moreover, after these evil persons die, they fall into the Avici hell, lying on their backs for nine hundred trillion years, lying on their faces for nine hundred trillion years, lying on the left side
(lying on the left side)
for nine hundred trillion years, lying on the right side
(lying on the right side)
for nine hundred trillion years, burning and charring
(the same as ‘scorched’)

upon the hot iron. Dying there, they are reborn in the roasting hell, the great roasting hell, the living hell, and the black-rope hell, experiencing all such suffering for the same number of years as above. Dying in the black-rope hell, they are reborn again in the great Avici hell.
Śāriputra,
for this reason, whether householders or home-leavers who draw near such a person
(the followers of these evil persons)
, and the good teachers
(good knowing companions, that is, the supporters of these evil persons)
and all the patrons
(the benefactors and patrons of these evil persons)
, in all six hundred forty trillion persons, together with these four teachers
(together with these four evil persons)
live and die together, and in the great hell undergo all manner of burning and boiling.
Thus, Śāriputra,
all the good-teacher households of such a person, all the patron households, disciples, teachers, and those who follow along — all who are counted in that number — are born in hell.

Śāriputra, you cannot know how many there are; only the Tathāgata can know. Those who with these evil persons fall into the great hell, living and dying together, number in all six hundred forty trillion persons; thus they revolve and suffer for one kalpa, remaining in hell until the conflagration of the great kalpa. Why? Śāriputra, to break the utmost, right, and perfect enlightenment of the Tathāgatas is an offense very heavy, not light. When the great kalpa burns, these four evil persons and the six hundred forty trillion persons pass from this Avici great hell and are reborn elsewhere, in the great hell. Why? Śāriputra, their heavy offenses being complete, their retribution is not small: in other regions, for countless hundreds of thousands of billions of na-yuta years they undergo great suffering. When the world comes into being again, these four evil persons and the six hundred forty trillion persons, together with the others whose offenses are not yet finished, at their death are reborn again in the great hell of this world.”

(Translation: These evil persons, destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha, also cause many who follow them to suffer great distress. Moreover, after these evil persons die, they fall into the Avici hell, lying on their backs upon the hot iron for nine hundred trillion years, on their faces for nine hundred trillion years, on the left side for nine hundred trillion years, and on the right side for nine hundred trillion years, burning and charring in the Avici hell. After dying in the Avici hell, they are reborn in the roasting hell, the great roasting hell, the living hell, and the black-rope hell, undergoing in each of these hells in turn the manifold suffering of lying on the back nine hundred trillion years, on the face nine hundred trillion years, on the left side nine hundred trillion years, and on the right side nine hundred trillion years. Finally, dying in the black-rope hell, they are reborn again into the great Avici hell to continue their suffering. Śāriputra, for this reason, all householders and home-leavers who draw near these four evil monks, and their close associates (good teachers), and their patrons (benefactors), in all six hundred forty trillion persons, live and die together with the four evil monks, fall together into hell, and undergo all manner of burning and boiling in the great hell. Thus, Śāriputra, all the supporters of these four evil monks, the households of all the patrons (benefactors), the disciples, the teachers, and those who follow along — all who are counted in that number — are born in hell. Śāriputra, you cannot know how many there are; only the Tathāgata can know. Those who with these four evil monks fall into the great hell, living and dying together, number in all six hundred forty trillion persons; thus they revolve and suffer for one great kalpa, remaining in hell until the conflagration of the kalpa. Why? Śāriputra, they break the utmost, right, and perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas — an offense very heavy, not light. If at the end of a corrupt kalpa the conflagration burns, these four evil monks and the six hundred forty trillion persons pass from this Avici great hell and are reborn in great hells elsewhere. Why? Śāriputra, their heavy offenses being complete, their retribution is not small: in the great hells of other regions, for countless hundreds of thousands of billions of na-yuta years they undergo great suffering. When this world again comes into being, these four evil monks and the six hundred forty trillion persons, together with the others whose offenses are not yet complete, at their death are reborn again into the great hell of this world.)
[Being the tiger’s ghost helper (
chang

)] To act as the tiger’s ghost helper. In old legend, a person eaten by a tiger becomes, after death, a ghost helper whose sole function is to lure people for the tiger to eat. [One kalpa] Here it refers to one great kalpa. A great kalpa contains the four intermediate kalpas of formation, abiding, destruction, and emptiness. At the end of the kalpa of destruction, the fire, water, and wind calamities necessarily arise.

blocks.text: Appendix One: This Undercurrent That the Buddhist Community Ought to Take Seriously

inline.s: Master Weixian

[Master Weixian] A native of Pengxi, Sichuan, he entered the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Academy at the age of fourteen and was highly esteemed by Master Taixu, his Buddhist learning being profound. In his youth he already had essays and treatises that made his name known throughout the Buddhist world. In the 1950s he was buffeted by political movements and imprisoned for twenty-six years, enduring great hardship. In prison he practiced diligently without cease and studied the Buddhist canon deeply. On his release in the 1980s he became the abbot of Chongqing Ciyun Temple and widely spread the good karmic conditions of the Dharma. With his profound learning he taught the Dharma and transmitted the precepts at monasteries at home and abroad, winning deep reverence throughout the Buddhist world. He served as chairman of the advisory committee of the Buddhist Association of China, president of the Chongqing Buddhist Association, and head of the Chongqing Buddhist Academy. He passed away at Tushan Temple in Nan’an District, Chongqing, at 4:50 a.m. on February 2, 2013, at the age of ninety-three.
[Note] This essay reveals that China’s Benyuan Dharma Gate, whether in doctrine or in funds, all derives from the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate,
and is a branch center of the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate:
More and more evidence shows that the impact of this undercurrent is by no means accidental or spontaneous,
but organized and planned,
backed both by
huge sums of money as its support,
and possessing channels and bases for
printing books and recording tapes,
and moreover possessing those who
preach and incite — monks, nuns, and laypersons and so on.
About two years ago (that is, 1997),
the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate got in touch with temples in Jiangxi; if a large ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ center could be established, it could remit ten million yuan.
These
“Benyuan Dharma Gate” centers

established with funds from the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate, because the name ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ is too notorious, now change to such brands as “relying on Master Shandao,” “promoting Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought,” “promoting Master Shandao’s Buddha-recitation Dharma Gate,” and the “Shandao school,” and try as far as possible to conceal their connection with the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate. These people, harboring a crooked heart and practicing deceit, think that all can be deceived and that no one in the world is as clever as they
(that there is no one in the world cleverer than me)
, not realizing that evil retribution is behind, coming one after another.
Master Shandao instructed: “What has come is true, and what is sincere is real. To make clear that the practice and understanding accomplished in body, speech, and mind of all sentient beings,
must be done with a true and genuine mind.

One must not outwardly manifest the appearance of virtue and diligent effort while inwardly harboring falsehood — greed, hatred, perversity, deceit, all manner of cunning — an evil nature hard to change, a matter like venomous snakes and scorpions. Though one sets body, speech, and mind in motion, it is called the goodness of mixed poison, and also called the practice of falsehood, not real karmic action. If one settles the mind and so practices, then even if one toils body and mind, day and night through the twelve hours, rushing and pushing as though one’s head were on fire, it is all
(with ‘all’ meaning ‘altogether’)
called the goodness of mixed poison.
To wish to turn back from this mixed-poison practice and seek rebirth in that Buddha’s Pure Land is entirely impossible.
” (The Four-Volume Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra)

[It is a branch center of the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate] Master Jingkong’s Questions and Answers in Buddhist Study, answering the seventy-fourth session of fellow practitioners visiting Hong Kong, contains this: “Q:
A home-leaver has recently been expounding the Dharma in various places around China, and is in fact promoting a heresy — the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate.
Their method is this: if a monastery is willing to publicize the Japanese Jōdo Shinshū for them, they invest ten million renminbi at one stroke.
. Second,
if a Chinese layperson is willing to publicize the Jōdo Shinshū for them on the internet, they can supply a monthly salary and bonus.

. The concrete way of working is that the Chinese layperson comes forward to establish a forum, and they assign a person on a full-time basis each day to repost the posts of the Japanese Jōdo Shinshū on the various Buddhist Pure Land forums.

If this Chinese layperson is very rich in Buddhist knowledge, they can supply a monthly salary of ten thousand renminbi (note: the layperson’s monthly salary is ten thousand renminbi; if it is a Dharma master, what monthly salary do they supply?)

. The Japanese demand is that this seller of Buddhism should pretend to be a devoted disciple of the Founding Master Yinguang, Master Jingkong, or an esoteric master, mix with ordinary Buddhist friends on the internet, and make everyone admire their Buddhist foundation, and then lead ordinary Buddhist friends to accept the views of the Japanese Jōdo Shinshū. On the above matters I ask the Elder Master to instruct.”

[Honganji] Honganji is the head temple of the Honganji branch of the Jōdo Shinshū of Japanese Buddhism. [Jōdo Shinshū] Also called the Benyuan school, it permits monks to take wives and bear children, and propagates the Benyuan Dharma Gate of “recitation of the name surely brings rebirth, the evil person is the true capacity.”
Lately, from Buddhist publications and from actual contact, there is reflected
an undercurrent in China’s Buddhist community of “studying Japanese Buddhism and taking the Japanese Buddhist road.”
This undercurrent impacts from two sides. The first is to destroy the fundamental rule of China’s Han Buddhism requiring that monks must “wear the robe, be vegetarian, and remain celibate.”

A fair number of Japanese home-leavers take wives and bear children, drink alcohol and eat meat, wear Western suits, and disregard the precepts, which greatly pleases our own monks who do not keep the precepts.
The essay The Alarm Bell (published in Taizhou Buddhism,
, no.
, issue no.
) exposes: “It is now found that in key temples of City
W

four young and middle-aged home-leavers have already returned to lay life, and the head of the fairly famous ‘Kairu Sutra-Printing Society’ — the monk Kairu of Mount Jiuhua — again returned to lay life last year.” It is reported that
in some coastal cities of our country monks are in the temple by day, and at night return to their own private dwellings to live a family life,
and the social impact is extremely bad.
